cells.uncertainty: Four positive-signal C JSON third-party paths pass two valid controls with format-aware tree results, parser source coverage and stable AFL++ feedback: jansson 2.15.1 (282,984 Debian popcon sourcemax installations), json-c 0.19 (269,736), cJSON 1.7.19 (150,958), yyjson 0.13.0 (14,868). They have separate parser sources. Debian installations mostly reflect dependencies and miss vendored copies. Search remains bounded to the recorded Conan recipe queries; four paths do not establish the definitive top ten or full RFC 8259 compliance. ISO C documents no JSON API.

Four independent C++ JSON parser families pass two valid controls and scoped parser source/AFL feedback. RapidJSON 1.1.0 is a 2016 release that needs Clang -fdelayed-template-parsing to build without source changes on this toolchain; this target uses AddressSanitizer and AFL++, without UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. Source-package installations favor runtime packages and undercount header-only libraries; RapidJSON is header-only with 899 Debian development-package installs. Six documentation leads remain unverified, including Boost.JSON. The search records 320 Debian source-name hits; no complete top-ten claim follows. JSON-specific use is unknown; valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Five Go JSON paths passed two valid structure-aware controls, source-scoped coverage and stable AFL++ feedback: json-iterator/go (18,454 Imported by), tidwall/gjson (10,420), ugorji/go/codec (10,142), goccy/go-json (4,192), and buger/jsonparser (2,171). GJSON and buger/jsonparser are path-query parsers, and their adapter traverses every value in the controls; buger/jsonparser is not claimed to validate an arbitrary complete JSON document. go-codec is multi-format: its Imported by count measures the package across several formats, not JSON-specific use. sonic (2,428) and three other numeric leads remain unverified, so the fifth path is not a definitive fifth most-used parser. Search is bounded to five pkg.go.dev queries of 100 results each. The Go standard encoding/json path is separate and unranked. Valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Pilot cell: ten JSON package/API paths are control-verified and runnable. Jackson databind and core share a tokenizer family; Gson, fastjson 1.x, org.json, fastjson2, json-simple, json-smart, Moshi, and Parsson are separate parser families. Fastjson 1.2.83 has its own DefaultJSONParser/JSONLexer; the com.alibaba:fastjson coordinate adoption metric sums both 1.x and later 2.x fastjson2 facade releases, so it is not a 1.x-only count. Its pinned-release direct-dependent count is separately recorded. Json-simple 1.1.1 is an older 2012 release with a high default-release count, so ranking uses the common deps.dev summed metric. Json-smart is verified on its RFC 4627 object/array mode, not scalar roots. Parsson implements Jakarta JSON-P with its own tokenizer over a local InputStream; the Jakarta API jar supplies interfaces. Three numeric leads remain unverified. Maven Central search is bounded to 100 hits per query (322 unique hits); deps.dev counts measure package adoption, not JSON-specific use. Two valid nested controls do not establish complete format coverage.

Pilot cell: five high-download package/API paths have valid nested-object and nested-array controls, package parser coverage, and AFL++ feedback; four independent parser families are represented. jsonparse (105,362,611 downloads) has no API in its README; Parser.write(Buffer) is evidenced by packaged examples and tests. The adapter requires one root and checks the parser stack and tokenizer state. JSONStream (56,299,470 downloads) is a separate stream API path over the same pinned jsonparse 1.3.1 tokenizer, not an independent engine. JSONStream.parse([]) emits one root according to packaged code and tests despite its README statement. Its private parser exposes no end-of-input completeness check: the adapter requires one emitted root, no error, and stream end, but trailing unfinished syntax after a complete root may go undetected. JSONStream own package source is covered; differential feedback on the valid controls arises only in underlying jsonparse source. @streamparser/json receives the entire Buffer and checks trailing bytes after the first root for whitespace. Other high-download leads use string-only APIs, superset grammars, or delegate to JSON.parse. Downloads cover 24 hand-picked candidates, not every search hit. Standard JSON.parse is separate. Two valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Four PHP JSON third-party paths passed valid nested object controls and source-line coverage. Laminas, JSON Machine and salsify also passed a valid nested array control and stable source-line AFL feedback. Laminas is abandoned, and its own decoder runs only when explicitly enabled; its default API route delegates to ext/json. JSON Machine shares ext/json for member decoding. salsify accepts only object/array roots and silently accepts concatenated documents, so its harness rejects anything other than one complete document; the tree-building listener is harness code. Four own-parser or partial-own-parser leads remain unverified; four json_decode wrappers are excluded. The bounded search used five Packagist queries of at most 100 hits each. Package downloads measure overall/historical adoption, not JSON parsing frequency. Valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Four positive-signal Python JSON third-party paths pass valid nested object and array controls with source-level parser coverage and AFL++ feedback: pydantic 2.14.3 (1,139,429,690 PyPI Stats last-month downloads), orjson 3.13.0 (218,014,317), simplejson 4.3.0 (49,365,386), and ijson 3.6.0 (46,615,664). Pydantic embeds Jiter; orjson shares the yyjson C syntax-parser family but this pilot measures its Rust deserializer, not vendored C source lines. ijson uses the asserted yajl2_c backend, with pinned YAJL C tokenizer and Python extension coverage; its source-built embedded YAJL -O0 route differs from the official Linux wheel linkage and optimisation, and its other backends are untested. PyPI package downloads include non-parse uses and transitive installs. Five targeted documented leads remain unverified; bounded PyPI Simple Index search has not yet been run. Python standard json is separately verified.

Nine verified Rust JSON parser paths selected within the first 100 hits of six crates.io queries (600 hits, 476 unique), captured 2026-11-17. Twelve documented leads remain unverified, including higher-download ijson (1,818,125) with unresolved shared-family status, so this is a bounded pilot rather than a complete top-ten ranking. Downloads are 90-day adoption proxies that include transitive pulls. gjson is a path-query parser: its parse/get calls assume valid input, so the adapter first calls its own whole-root valid function and then traverses every child through Value::each. The Rust and Go tidwall GJSON packages share design/maintainer lineage but have separate source implementations. Two small valid controls establish only their observed RFC 8259 structure; duplicate keys, huge numbers, deep nesting and non-UTF-8 are untested.

One verified path; no padding. Search is a substring match over all Homebrew formula names and descriptions for seven queries, captured 2026-11-17; it misses header-only decoders that are not packaged there. minimp3 and dr_mp3 have no value on the primary metric, so their GitHub stars are recorded as supplemental only and are not compared with Homebrew counts. libmad is an unresolved independent family. Homebrew installs measure macOS/Linux package demand for the whole mpg123 distribution (player and library), not direct use of the decoding API. libmpg123 is the same engine counted under mp3_id3v2/c. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

One verified path; no padding. Search is a substring match over all Homebrew formula names and descriptions for six queries, captured 2026-11-17; header-only C++ decoders and vcpkg/Conan packages were not searched. Homebrew installs measure demand for the whole TagLib distribution, mostly as a tag library, not use of its MPEG property API. TagLib parses frame headers and does not decode audio; for CBR streams without Xing/VBRI its duration comes from stream size and the first frame's bitrate. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

One verified path; no padding. Search is bounded by five pkg.go.dev queries at 100 hits each. Leads in leads.json are not verified parsers. Two valid controls do not establish complete Layer III support or independence from the mp3_id3v2 go-mp3 entry.

Pilot cell: only the highest-adoption pure-Java Layer III path was built and control-verified; no padding. Maven Central Solr search ranks by relevance, the phrase queries 'mp3 decoder' and 'mpeg audio' returned 0 hits, so leads were looked up directly on deps.dev and logged in leads.json. deps.dev public coverage is incomplete and jcodec's count covers the whole codec library, not MP3 use alone. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, MPEG-2.5 or intensity-stereo support; jcodec's Mp3Decoder throws on intensity stereo by design. Java SE 25 exports no MP3 API, so the standard count is zero by inventory.

One verified path; no padding. Search is six npm queries of 100 hits each, captured 2026-11-17; downloads were fetched for 15 hand-picked candidates, not every hit. mediabunny was found by `mp3 frame`, `mp3 duration` and `mp3 demuxer`, not the narrower queries. Its download count covers the whole media toolkit (muxing, conversion, many containers), not MP3 demuxing alone. The path demuxes frames and reads headers but does not decode Layer III audio (that would need WebCodecs). mediabunny is not among the mp3_id3v2/javascript paths; music-metadata and the mpg123 WASM wrappers are recorded as shared-family leads. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support. No standard Node.js MP3 API exists.

One verified path; no padding. Search is seven Packagist search.json queries capped at 50 hits each, captured 2026-11-17; package descriptions alone decided most exclusions. Packagist total downloads count Composer installs of the whole package (and wrappers pull getID3 transitively), not use of the MPEG frame parser. getID3 reads the first frame header, checks sync on following frames, and derives CBR duration from audio-data bytes and the header bitrate; it does not decode audio or report a frame count on these controls. Mp3Info, PHP-MP3 (falahati/php-mp3), the Zend media reader and fobilow/mp3file are unresolved independent candidates. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Two verified paths; no padding. The name search is a substring filter over the PyPI Simple index (serial 43764887) captured 2026-11-17; the 'mp3' and 'mpeg' hit lists were not triaged one by one, and download numbers were fetched only for 13 named candidates, so a less obvious frame parser could be missed. Native wrappers (av, soundfile, audioread, pygame, pymediainfo, miniaudio) are unresolved, not rejected: their parsers are real but outside Python source coverage. eyed3, hachoir and pymp3 are unresolved pure-Python leads. Mutagen reads headers and checks frame syncs but does not decode audio; for CBR streams without Xing/Info/VBRI its duration is stream bytes divided by the first header's bitrate. TinyTag also only reads headers: after five equal-bitrate frames it estimates duration from stream size and mean frame length, and it does not expose MPEG version, layer or frame count. Both full-length controls run the same TinyTag lines; its feedback difference is shown with a valid three-frame prefix of the 44.1 kHz control. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Pilot cell: one verified path, chosen as the highest crates.io 90-day download count (10,651,437) among hits that contain an MPEG audio frame parser. The facade crate symphonia (11,469,426) ranks higher but re-exports the same family. 11 frame-level leads remain unverified, so the count of one reflects pilot scope, not a search result. Search covers only the first 100 hits of six queries (591 hits, 350 unique) captured 2026-11-17; the 'mp3' query alone reports 1119 matches. Recent downloads include transitive dependency pulls (Symphonia is a dependency of rodio and others) and are an adoption proxy, not evidence of direct MP3 parsing use. Two untagged CBR controls (MPEG-1 44.1 kHz mono, MPEG-2 22.05 kHz stereo) do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Pilot cell: two third-party paths (expat 2.10.0 and libxml2 2.15.4) were built, matched the exact namespace-resolved summary of both valid controls under LLVM source coverage, and have native AFL++ feedback with a stable valid-control differential. They are distinct parser families. expat leads libxml2 by 6,410 installs (2.2%) on the binary-package metric, a near tie. The Debian sourcemax table would invert the order (libxml2 source 61,109) only because the libxml2 source now builds libxml2-16 and the older libxml2 binary is no longer attributed to it, so binary runtime-library counts are the primary metric; libxml2-16 (9,413) is not added because hosts may have both. Popcon counts installations, mostly pulled in as dependencies, not direct parser use. Search was the Conan Center recipe-name substring 'xml' (9 hits, 1 of them a C XML parser) plus seven targeted C names; Conan and Debian miss vendored single-file parsers. The control oracle (controls/xml/check_controls.py) uses Python's pyexpat, the same family as expat but not libxml2, so the libxml2 match is a cross-family check. The expat harness pins XML_SetHashSalt so AFL++ maps are reproducible; libxml2 needed no such change. ISO C documents no XML API. Two valid UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity, encoding, XML 1.1 or rejection behaviour.

Three C++ XML paths are verified on a namespace-aware valid control, with source coverage and AFL feedback. TinyXML2 also passed a second valid control that omits a processing instruction; TinyXML2 11.0.0 rejects the same processing instruction in the shared order control. Both TinyXML2 and pugixml preserve qualified names but leave namespace resolution to the adapters, which is explicitly separated from library parsing. libxml++ remains unresolved and shares the libxml2 C parser family. The bounded search compared four named format-specific libraries using Debian -dev installs; Homebrew install-on-request gives a different order. Whole frameworks are not ranked by framework-wide installs. Two small valid UTF-8 controls cannot establish complete XML 1.0, DTD/entity, encoding or malformed-input behavior.

Pilot cell: the two highest Imported-by XML parser leads (etree 2,098; xmlquery 627) were built and control-verified. Both use the Go encoding/xml Decoder tokenizer, but build distinct trees. 14 further numeric leads remain unresolved and are not selected or ranked. The first 100 hits of six queries were captured (xml dom returned 68; xml reader 28). The two small valid UTF-8 XML 1.0 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity declaration, non-UTF-8 encoding, XML 1.1, or attribute-value normalization behaviour.

Five third-party XML package paths are verified and runnable: Jackson XML, Xerces2-J, Woodstox, dom4j, and Aalto. Xerces2-J, Woodstox, and Aalto are independent tokenizer/parser engines. Jackson XML is a format-specific token projection over pinned Woodstox; its own module and the underlying Woodstox parser have separate source coverage. Its ordered token output retains decoded field/value text but omits namespace URIs, root name, comments, processing instructions, and attribute-versus-child origin. dom4j builds a tree over the default JAXP SAX parser (OpenJDK Xerces fork), with dom4j and underlying JDK coverage separately recorded. The standard javax.xml.parsers path is counted separately and shares the Xerces2-J family. Nine documentation leads remain unresolved; legacy dom4j:dom4j is not counted beside org.dom4j:dom4j. Maven Central search is relevance-ranked and bounded to 100 hits per query (345 unique hits); deps.dev sums direct dependents per release and does not measure XML-specific use or independent parser families. Two small UTF-8 XML 1.0 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, external-entity, schema, non-UTF-8, or XML 1.1 behavior.

Pilot cell: saxes 6.0.0, sax 1.6.1, fast-xml-parser 5.12.1, @xmldom/xmldom 0.9.12, and xml2js 0.6.2 are control-verified, source-covered, and have input-dependent AFL++ feedback. Comparable 30-day npm downloads rank the five package paths; counts include transitive adoption. saxes and sax share historical fork lineage but have distinct parser code. fast-xml-parser has its own scanner and validator but no namespace URI resolution, so the adapter resolves expanded names over its qualified names and xmlns attributes. @xmldom/xmldom has its own XMLReader tokenizer and DOM builder, accepts locally decoded text, and the adapter treats every warning or error as fatal. xml2js builds an ordered tree over the same pinned sax 1.6.1 tokenizer as the selected sax path; it drops comments and processing instructions, which can merge adjacent text segments. Its own package and underlying sax source coverage are recorded separately. jsdom remains an unverified route sharing the saxes family. The search is bounded to recorded queries and snapshot; two valid controls do not establish complete XML 1.0 compliance.

Pilot cell, one verified third-party path. The earlier zero count wrongly excluded libxml2-family wrappers; PROTOCOL.md lets a wrapper qualify as a package API with its parser family identified, so sabre/xml is counted with family libxml2 (shared with the standard XMLReader path). symfony/dom-crawler and jms/serializer stay excluded because they only navigate or map an already parsed DOM/SimpleXML tree. The other libxml2-family wrappers (veewee/xml, mtownsend/xml-to-array, saloonphp/xml-wrangler, laravie/parser, orchestra/parser, pear/xml_parser and smaller ones) were not evaluated by the cutoff and remain unresolved, as do the own-code leads prewk/xml-string-streamer and watoki/dom. sabre/xml drops xmlns declarations and text in mixed-content elements by design, so its summary omits namespace declaration counts. Its coverage image uses Ubuntu PHP 8.5.4 with libxml 2.15.2; its AFL++ overlay uses the source-built PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4. The search covers the first 100 hits of five Packagist queries; controls are two small UTF-8 namespace-aware documents without DOCTYPE.

Two verified third-party paths (lxml and xmltodict) are selected from nine named PyPI/project-documentation leads. A bounded PyPI Simple Index search remains pending; seven leads are unresolved, so this is not a completed top-ten ranking. lxml uses source-built libxml2 2.15.4; xmltodict and the standard ElementTree path use Expat. Both lxml controls exercise valid UTF-8 XML 1.0 namespace structures without DOCTYPE, not full XML conformance. PyPI Stats package downloads are not XML-specific use. lxml AFL feedback excludes parser.c lines 8700-8720 because address-sensitive attribute hash lookups varied across identical valid replays.

Four verified XML parser implementations selected within the first 100 hits of seven crates.io queries (642 hits, 483 unique), captured 2026-11-17. Twelve documented leads remain unverified. The xml-rs 1.0.0 package has 32,180,109 recent downloads but is a compatibility re-export of the xml package, so it is excluded as a duplicate family. Downloads include transitive pulls and are adoption proxies; ranks compare selected independent paths only. The xmlparser tokenizer does not resolve namespaces or validate tree structure; its adapter provides those observations. Two small UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, external entity, non-UTF-8 encoding, XML 1.1, or redundant namespace redeclaration behavior. RustyXML 0.3.0 passed valid-control parsing but exact repeatable AFL++ feedback was not established; see data/rust/xml/rustyxml-feedback-audit.md.
